document_metadata.title: 105、INT. GRAND BALLROOM - EVE
document_metadata.summary: Marianne is devastated as Willoughby coldly rejects her and joins his party; Elinor and Mrs. Jennings help her leave, while Lucy and Robert offer to escort them, amid gossiping onlookers.

entities.name: Marianne calls out to Willoughby across the room
entities.description: In a brief lull in the noise, Marianne shouts Willoughby's name, drawing everyone's attention as she rushes toward him with outstretched arms, visibly joyful.

entities.name: Willoughby hesitates to embrace Marianne
entities.description: When Marianne approaches with open arms, Willoughby remains stiff and unresponsive, only reluctantly shaking her hand after she questions him, visibly uncomfortable under the scrutiny of others.

entities.name: Marianne confronts Willoughby about his absence
entities.description: Marianne, distressed by Willoughby's cold behavior, urgently asks him why he never visited her, whether he was in London, and if he received her letters, pleading for an explanation.

entities.name: Willoughby gives a strained response to Marianne
entities.description: Willoughby, visibly sweating and tense, offers a formal and awkward reply, acknowledging receipt of Marianne's messages but avoiding any emotional engagement.

entities.name: Onlookers observe Marianne and Willoughby's encounter
entities.description: As Marianne and Willoughby speak, many people in the room surreptitiously watch the interaction, including Mrs. Jennings, who comments on it to Fanny and John, and Lucy, who whispers to Robert as they pass by.

entities.summary: A reclusive former soldier and friend of Sir John, connected to the East India Regiment, arrives late to a gathering, is moved by Marianne's singing, and silently offers her his knife, drawing admiration for his worldly demeanor.

entities.name: Edward
entities.description: A clergyman in parson's garb, present at the wedding and emerging from the church with Elinor.
entities.summary: Fanny's elder brother, expected from Plymouth, is visiting soon, prompting Margaret to vacate her room; his arrival is anticipated by the household and linked to housing prospects discussed with Elinor, while interactions around Fanny reflect ongoing family adjustments following recent loss.

entities.description: A participant in the wedding festivities, recognizable by her gigantic mauve bonnet.
entities.summary: A sociable, inquisitive woman accompanying Sir John Middleton shows concern for the Dashwoods, engages in dinner conversations about romance, notes Colonel Brandon's absence, and assists with packing after a picnic.

entities.name: Mr Palmer
entities.description: A guest at the wedding, present with Charlotte.
entities.summary: A reserved, sarcastic man, husband of Charlotte Palmer, is emotionally detached, objects to her plans, hides behind a newspaper, and visits Devonshire to see the Dashwood sisters, while briefly joining the Colonel in the billiard room.

entities.name: Sir John Middleton
entities.description: A guest attending the wedding ceremony outside the church.
entities.summary: A man of narrative importance seeks Mrs Dashwood, while another, jovial and friendly, joins Mrs Jennings and shares camaraderie with Colonel Brandon, assisting at gatherings and engaging in leisure activities with the family.

entities.name: Mrs. Dashwood
entities.description: A guest at the wedding, present among the principals of the story.
entities.summary: Mrs. Dashwood, mother of Elinor, Marianne, and Margaret, supports her family through emotional transitions, present in key moments including her husband's death, housing decisions, and family gatherings, while navigating grief and displacement.

entities.name: Margaret Dashwood
entities.description: A young member of the wedding party, present among the principals.
entities.summary: A young, perceptive Dashwood daughter resists changes from John and Fanny's arrival, hides to avoid Fanny, and is concerned over displaced belongings; her toys are removed by Elinor and Marianne amid room preparations for Edward.

entities.name: Thomas
entities.description: A member of the wedding party, present among the principals.
entities.summary: A servant at Norland Park who assists the Dashwoods, carries luggage, announces arrivals, and tends to Bedivere, including holding the horse's reins before Willoughby takes them.

entities.name: John
entities.description: A guest at the wedding, present alongside Fanny.
entities.summary: A man arrives at Norland with Fanny to fulfill his father's wish by providing financial support to four women, marking a shift in household authority due to inheritance.

entities.name: Fanny Dashwood
entities.description: A guest dressed in an inappropriate outfit who is struck in the eye by a sixpence and falls into a gorse bush.
entities.summary: John Dashwood's wife, concerned about finances and inheritance, questions supporting his mother and sisters, reflecting on duty and the limits of financial responsibility after moving into Norland.
